---
name: specdex
description: Read-only lookup, citation, impact and consistency checks for this project's BMAD specifications (PRD and addendum, UX DESIGN.md and EXPERIENCE.md, architecture spine, specs, preview tickets). Use when an answer depends on what the specs say or where - an ID such as FR-12, NFR-3, UJ-2, AD-7 or CQ-4, a section such as "prd §4.2", wording to locate, every place that cites an ID, what a change touches, dangling or out-of-range references, or which requirements tickets, architecture or UX cover - and use it before grep or reading whole spec files. It never edits specs.
---

# specdex

## Overview

This skill returns the exact spec unit an answer needs, with its `path:start-end` range and labels that say whether the text is current. It costs a fraction of the tokens of reading files and keeps trail or historical text from being quoted as a current requirement. Act as a careful spec librarian: cite what the record says, and say plainly when the index cannot answer.

## On Activation

```text
python3 {skill-root}/scripts/specdex.py [--json] [--project DIR] <command> ...
```

`{skill-root}` is the folder holding this file. It needs Python 3.11+ and nothing else; if `python3` is older, use `uv run {skill-root}/scripts/specdex.py`. Run it from inside the project (it walks up to the BMAD project root, failing that the git root) or pass `--project`. Global options go before the command. The project overlay `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/specdex-overlay.toml` is picked up when present. The first call builds the index in a second or two; every later call re-hashes the files and reindexes only what changed, so an answer reflects the files as they were at that call.

## Pick the command

| The question has | Run |
|---|---|
| An ID: FR-12, AD-3, UJ-2, a glossary term, a design token | `resolve FR-12` for where it is defined, its positional items and its elaborations; `get FR-12` for the text |
| A heading, `doc §n`, `path:line`, `path:a-b` or `path#Heading` | `get "prd §4.2"` |
| Wording or a paraphrase | `search <words>`, then `get` the top hit's reference (`--expand 1` inlines it) |
| "All" or "every" place citing X | `refs FR-12`: includes lines inside ranges such as FR-9–FR-12; `--children` adds FR-12.k, `--kind binds` narrows |
| The shape of a document | `outline [file] --level 2` |
| A change to review | `diff <old-rev> [<new-rev>]` (default new: the worktree; flags shifted FR-n.k lists and added IDs already in the file's history), then `impact <ID or path:a-b>`, then `lint` |
| Tickets | `covers` checks every ticket's covers chain; `coverage --by tickets\|architecture\|ux [--only gaps]` |
| Whether specdex can be trusted here | `status` |

One unit answers what it says, not what other units add. When the question is about a concept other rules may also constrain (who owns something, a limit, an exception, whether something exists at all), also `search` the concept's key term before answering, and say which units you checked.

`get` takes several references in one call; `--budget N` gives each reference about N tokens (estimated as characters/4) and never cuts a single unit. Paths are project-relative; cite them exactly as printed. `get`, `outline` and `impact` also accept any unique path suffix; `refs` takes an ID.

`--scope` chooses which files count: `record` (default) is the specs of record; `current` adds rationale and tickets; `rationale`, `trail`, `memlog` and `all` reach the history. Stay on the default unless the question is about why or when something was decided.

## Read the output

Each hit starts `path:start-end [labels] — heading path`. Labels read `[role; temporal; decision: ...; flags; authority]`, with the parts that apply:

- **role**: `record` is the current spec of record, the only text that states current requirements. `ambiguous` is one of several candidate documents of one type with no overlay choice between them. `rationale` explains current decisions but requires nothing. `ticket`, `noncurrent` (an older document of a type that was not selected), `trail` (reviews, drafts, discussions), `memlog` and `unverified` (no rule matched) are not current requirements.
- **historical**: text kept as history inside a record, such as declined proposals, retired claims, or change requests as raised. It is true about the past, not about now.
- **decision: X**: on a change-request row, the decision taken. The decision is current; the request text is not.
- **flags** such as `assumption`, `note-for-pm`, `non-goal`, `conditional`: the unit is provisional or deliberately out of scope; say so when citing it.
- **superseded by prd [except ...]**: the PRD wins over this file, except in the named sections, which show `authoritative exception (...)`.

Quote only `record` text without `historical` as a current requirement, and cite it as `path:start-end` with its labels.

Statuses in `resolve`, `refs`, `impact` and `lint`:

- `defined`: exactly one definition.
- `ambiguous`: several definitions or candidate documents. Do not pick one; report them. When the definitions sit in different document scopes (AD in two spines, CAP in two specs), the citing document decides; otherwise suggest choosing the record in the overlay's `[current] records`.
- `out-of-bounds`: a positional ID past the end of its list (FR-12.9 when FR-12 has 5 items); the note gives the count.
- `not defined` or `unresolved`: a dangling reference.
- `historical only` (in `resolve`; `historical` in `refs` and `lint`): the ID is defined only in history, such as a retired or declined section. A current line citing it is a finding.
- `elaborated only`: elaborated somewhere but not defined in its owner document.
- `textual`: a phrase such as "all MVP FRs" may bind the ID; read the line to decide.

An empty answer says `none in a fully indexed scope`, which is a real negative, or `unknown (...)`, which is not: part of the scope could not be indexed. Every output ends with `generation <hash>`, the verified index state the answer came from.

`lint` is mechanical: duplicates, dangling or out-of-range references, unknown tokens, missing companions, replica drift, and BMAD's own spine validator. A validator that could not run (missing, changed since the profile was built, failed, or a revision snapshot) appears as a `validator-not-run` or `validator-failed` finding, never as silence. Its last lines say what it did not check: a clean lint does not mean the specs agree, and contradictions in meaning still need reading.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Done |
| 1 | Findings: `resolve` not `defined`, `lint` high severity, `coverage` gaps, `covers` problems |
| 2 | Usage error, unknown reference or scope, or the files kept changing during the call |
| 3 | Configuration or source error: unreadable profile or overlay, unreadable git revision |

## When to fall back

Say that specdex could not answer and use `rg -n` over the output folder (usually `_bmad-output/`) plus bounded reads of the matching section when:

- it exits 3;
- `status` shows `diagnostic unsupported-layout` (sharded v6 `index.md`, initiative-v7 folders) or `ambiguous-current`;
- `status` shows no `record` files: specdex found no specs where the profile looks, so its negatives mean nothing;
- an empty answer is `unknown (...)`;
- `search` misses a paraphrase after one retry with other words.

`status` showing `profile ... (unverified)` means the installed BMAD differs from the version the profile was built for; results still come, but check surprising ones by reading.

## Read-only

specdex never writes inside the project and refuses an index location inside it; the index lives in the user cache, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/specdex/` (default `$HOME/.cache/specdex/`), or at `--db`. It reports evidence; changing a spec is the owning BMAD skill's job: `bmad-prd` for the PRD and addendum, `bmad-ux` for DESIGN.md and EXPERIENCE.md, `bmad-architecture` for the spine, `bmad-spec` for specs, `bmad-preview-ticketing` for tickets, `bmad-correct-course` for a change across documents. After such an edit, `impact` and `lint` show what else needs attention. The overlay is the project's configuration; edit it only when the user asks.

"""Open a verified index generation.

Worktree mode hashes every in-scope file on every open and re-extracts what
changed before answering (mtime and size are never trusted). Snapshot mode
indexes one commit's blobs; a commit is immutable, so a complete snapshot index
needs no re-verification. The two modes use different cache files and never mix.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import sqlite3
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from . import __version__, extract, resolve, store
from .config import Config, ConfigError
from .sources import GitRevisionSource, SourceFile, WorktreeSource


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Index:
    conn: sqlite3.Connection
    config: Config
    mode: str            # "worktree" or "commit:<sha>"
    generation: str
    changed: int         # files re-extracted while opening
    verify_ms: float
    update_ms: float


def cache_path(config: Config, mode: str) -> Path:
    base = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_CACHE_HOME", Path.home() / ".cache")) / "specdex"
    key = hashlib.sha256(f"{config.project_root.resolve()}|{mode}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
    return base / key / "index.sqlite"


def index_file(config: Config, mode: str, db_path: Path | None) -> Path:
    """An explicit --db holds the worktree index; each revision snapshot gets a sibling file, so two never share one.
    The index never goes inside the project, whatever --db or XDG_CACHE_HOME say: specdex writes nothing there."""
    if db_path is None:
        path = cache_path(config, mode)
    elif mode == WorktreeSource.label:
        path = db_path
    else:
        path = db_path.with_name(f"{db_path.stem}.{mode.replace(':', '-')}{db_path.suffix}")
    if path.resolve().is_relative_to(config.project_root.resolve()):
        raise ConfigError(f"index location {path} is inside the project; use --db or XDG_CACHE_HOME outside it")
    return path


def open_index(config: Config, revision: str | None = None, db_path: Path | None = None) -> Index:
    source = GitRevisionSource(config, revision) if revision else WorktreeSource(config)
    mode = source.label
    conn = store.connect(index_file(config, mode, db_path))
    stamp = f"{store.SCHEMA_VERSION}|{config.fingerprint}|{__version__}"
    started = time.perf_counter()
    # Every return leaves one read transaction open: all of a command's queries see the same generation.
    if revision and store.get_meta(conn, "stamp") == stamp and store.get_meta(conn, "complete") == "1" and store.get_meta(conn, "mode") == mode:
        conn.execute("BEGIN")
        return Index(conn, config, mode, store.get_meta(conn, "generation") or "", 0, 0.0, 0.0)
    inventory = source.files()
    verified = time.perf_counter()
    conn.execute("BEGIN")
    if _fresh(conn, stamp, inventory, source.problems):
        return Index(conn, config, mode, store.get_meta(conn, "generation") or "", 0, (verified - started) * 1000, 0.0)
    conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    changed = 0
    try:
        inventory = source.files()  # re-read under the lock: the first read may predate another writer's commit
        if not _fresh(conn, stamp, inventory, source.problems):
            changed = _sync(conn, config, stamp, inventory)
            resolve.derive(conn, config, source.problems)
            store.set_meta(conn, "generation", _generation(config, inventory))
            store.set_meta(conn, "stamp", stamp)
            store.set_meta(conn, "complete", "1")
            store.set_meta(conn, "mode", mode)
            store.set_meta(conn, "source_problems", json.dumps(source.problems))
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    done = time.perf_counter()
    conn.execute("BEGIN")
    return Index(conn, config, mode, store.get_meta(conn, "generation") or "", changed, (verified - started) * 1000, (done - verified) * 1000)


def _fresh(conn: sqlite3.Connection, stamp: str, inventory: dict[str, SourceFile], problems: list) -> bool:
    if store.get_meta(conn, "stamp") != stamp or store.get_meta(conn, "complete") != "1":
        return False
    if store.get_meta(conn, "source_problems") != json.dumps(problems):
        return False
    stored = {row["path"]: (row["sha256"], row["identity"]) for row in conn.execute("SELECT path, sha256, identity FROM files")}
    return stored == {path: (source.sha256, source.identity) for path, source in inventory.items()}


def _generation(config: Config, inventory: dict[str, SourceFile]) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256(config.fingerprint.encode())
    for path in sorted(inventory):
        digest.update(f"{path}\0{inventory[path].sha256}\n".encode())
    return digest.hexdigest()[:12]


def _sync(conn: sqlite3.Connection, config: Config, stamp: str, inventory: dict[str, SourceFile]) -> int:
    if store.get_meta(conn, "stamp") != stamp:
        store.reset(conn)
    stored = {row["path"]: (row["sha256"], row["identity"]) for row in conn.execute("SELECT path, sha256, identity FROM files")}
    skipped = _not_extracted(config, inventory)
    stale = [p for p in stored if p not in inventory or stored[p] != (inventory[p].sha256, inventory[p].identity)
             or (p in skipped) != _was_skipped(conn, p)]
    for path in stale:
        store.delete_file(conn, path)
    remaining = set(stored) - set(stale)
    changed = 0
    for path, source in sorted(inventory.items()):
        if path in remaining:
            continue
        text = source.data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        facts = None if path in skipped else extract.extract(config, path, text)
        store.write_file(conn, source, text, facts)
        changed += 1
    return changed


def _was_skipped(conn: sqlite3.Connection, path: str) -> bool:
    row = conn.execute("SELECT extracted FROM files WHERE path=?", (path,)).fetchone()
    return bool(row) and not row["extracted"]


def _not_extracted(config: Config, inventory: dict[str, SourceFile]) -> set[str]:
    """Paths indexed only as aliases: symlinks to an indexed file and equal declared replicas.
    A drifting replica is not an alias: it stays a separate document and lint reports the drift."""
    skipped = {p for p, s in inventory.items() if s.is_link and s.identity in inventory}
    for group in config.replicas:
        primary = inventory.get(group[0])
        for member in group[1:]:
            if primary and member in inventory and inventory[member].sha256 == primary.sha256:
                skipped.add(member)
    return skipped
"""SQLite store: per-file facts plus derived (whole-corpus) tables.

Per-file tables are replaced when a file changes; derived tables are rebuilt by
resolve.derive() in the same transaction, so readers always see one coherent
generation. The database is a disposable cache: deleting it loses nothing.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

from .config import ConfigError
from .extract import FileFacts
from .sources import SourceFile

SCHEMA_VERSION = 4  # stored in PRAGMA user_version; a different value rebuilds the tables
APPLICATION_ID = 0x53445831  # "SDX1" in PRAGMA application_id: marks a file as a specdex index

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meta(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS files(
  path TEXT PRIMARY KEY, sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, size INTEGER, identity TEXT, is_link INTEGER,
  artifact TEXT, kind TEXT, scope_kind TEXT, lines INTEGER, frontmatter TEXT, text TEXT,
  extracted INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  role TEXT, canonical TEXT, companion_of TEXT, superseded_by TEXT, authority_note TEXT);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS spans(
  sid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, path TEXT, ord INTEGER, kind TEXT, start INTEGER, end INTEGER, level INTEGER,
  title TEXT, hpath TEXT, temporal TEXT, flags TEXT, disposition TEXT);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS spans_path ON spans(path, ord);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS chunks(cid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, path TEXT, sid INTEGER, start INTEGER, end INTEGER, hpath TEXT, body TEXT, terms TEXT);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS chunks_path ON chunks(path);
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS chunks_fts USING fts5(
  hpath, body, terms, content='chunks', content_rowid='cid', tokenize='porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2');
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS occ(
  oid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, path TEXT, line INTEGER, col INTEGER, family TEXT, id TEXT, raw TEXT,
  via_range INTEGER, sid INTEGER, kind TEXT, src_id TEXT, rule TEXT, derived INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  target INTEGER, status TEXT);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS occ_id ON occ(id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS occ_path ON occ(path, line);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cand(
  cid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, path TEXT, role TEXT, id TEXT, family TEXT, shape TEXT, sid INTEGER, line INTEGER,
  parent_id TEXT, ordinal INTEGER);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS cand_path ON cand(path);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS defs(
  did INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, id TEXT, family TEXT, scope TEXT, path TEXT, line INTEGER, sid INTEGER, shape TEXT,
  effective TEXT, parent_id TEXT, ordinal INTEGER);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS defs_id ON defs(id);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS poscount(path TEXT, parent_id TEXT, n INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS backtick(path TEXT, line INTEGER, col INTEGER, word TEXT, sid INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS companions(path TEXT, value TEXT, line INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fdiag(path TEXT, code TEXT, severity TEXT, line INTEGER, detail TEXT);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS gdiag(code TEXT, severity TEXT, path TEXT, line INTEGER, detail TEXT);
"""

PER_FILE_TABLES = ("spans", "occ", "cand", "poscount", "backtick", "companions", "fdiag")


def connect(path: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=60, isolation_level=None)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    outdated = conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0] != SCHEMA_VERSION
    if outdated and not _is_ours(conn):  # checked before any PRAGMA that would change a foreign file
        conn.close()
        raise ConfigError(f"{path} is not a specdex index; refusing to rebuild it (choose another --db)")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL")
    if outdated:
        _create_schema(conn)
    return conn


def _is_ours(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> bool:
    """Empty, marked as specdex, or an index from before the marker (it has specdex's meta and chunks tables)."""
    if conn.execute("PRAGMA application_id").fetchone()[0] == APPLICATION_ID:
        return True
    tables = {row[0] for row in conn.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")}
    return not tables or {"meta", "chunks", "files"} <= tables


def _create_schema(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    """Drop whatever an older version left and create the current tables, in one transaction."""
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        if conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0] != SCHEMA_VERSION:  # another process may have won
            names = [row[0] for row in conn.execute(
                "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' AND name NOT LIKE 'chunks_fts_%'")]
            for name in names:
                conn.execute(f'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "{name}"')
            for statement in filter(str.strip, SCHEMA.split(";")):
                conn.execute(statement)
            conn.execute(f"PRAGMA user_version={SCHEMA_VERSION}")
            conn.execute(f"PRAGMA application_id={APPLICATION_ID}")
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise


def get_meta(conn: sqlite3.Connection, key: str) -> str | None:
    row = conn.execute("SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key=?", (key,)).fetchone()
    return row["value"] if row else None


def set_meta(conn: sqlite3.Connection, key: str, value: str) -> None:
    conn.execute("INSERT INTO meta(key, value) VALUES(?, ?) ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value=excluded.value", (key, value))


def reset(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    """Drop every row (used when the schema, profile or overlay changed)."""
    for table in ("files", "chunks", "defs", "gdiag", "meta") + PER_FILE_TABLES:
        conn.execute(f"DELETE FROM {table}")
    conn.execute("INSERT INTO chunks_fts(chunks_fts) VALUES('rebuild')")


def delete_file(conn: sqlite3.Connection, path: str) -> None:
    for table in PER_FILE_TABLES:
        conn.execute(f"DELETE FROM {table} WHERE path=?", (path,))
    rows = conn.execute("SELECT cid, hpath, body, terms FROM chunks WHERE path=?", (path,)).fetchall()
    for row in rows:
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO chunks_fts(chunks_fts, rowid, hpath, body, terms) VALUES('delete', ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                     (row["cid"], row["hpath"], row["body"], row["terms"]))
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM chunks WHERE path=?", (path,))
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM files WHERE path=?", (path,))
"""Command-line interface. Every command is read-only with respect to the project."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from . import __version__, render
from .config import ConfigError, load
from .index import open_index
from .queries import NotFound, Queries, StaleIndex
from .sources import SourceError

SKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DEFAULT_PROFILE = SKILL_ROOT / "profiles" / "bmad-6.13.0-next.toml"
DEFAULT_OVERLAY = Path("_bmad/custom/specdex-overlay.toml")
EXIT_OK, EXIT_FINDINGS, EXIT_USAGE, EXIT_CONFIG = 0, 1, 2, 3
CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4


def find_project_root(start: Path) -> Path:
    for candidate in [start, *start.parents]:
        if (candidate / "_bmad").is_dir():
            return candidate
    for candidate in [start, *start.parents]:
        if (candidate / ".git").exists():
            return candidate
    return start


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="specdex", description="Read-only search and checks for BMAD specifications.")
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"specdex {__version__}")
    parser.add_argument("--project", type=Path, help="project root (default: nearest folder with _bmad/)")
    parser.add_argument("--profile", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_PROFILE, help="BMAD profile TOML")
    parser.add_argument("--overlay", type=Path, help=f"project overlay TOML (default: {DEFAULT_OVERLAY} if present)")
    parser.add_argument("--rev", help="index this git revision (committed-snapshot mode) instead of the worktree")
    parser.add_argument("--db", type=Path, help="worktree index file; revision snapshots go next to it (default: under ~/.cache/specdex)")
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="JSON output")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    sub.add_parser("status", help="index generation, roles, profile binding, diagnostics")
    p = sub.add_parser("outline", help="heading tree with line ranges")
    p.add_argument("target", nargs="?", help="file path or suffix (default: all record files)")
    p.add_argument("--level", type=int, help="deepest heading level to show")
    p = sub.add_parser("resolve", help="where an ID, glossary term or token is defined and elaborated")
    p.add_argument("id")
    p.add_argument("--text", action="store_true", help="include the definition text")
    p = sub.add_parser("get", help="complete unit text: ID, term, token, path:line, path:start-end or path#heading")
    p.add_argument("ref", nargs="+")
    p.add_argument("--budget", type=int, default=2000, help="output budget in tokens (a single unit is never cut)")
    p = sub.add_parser("refs", help="every line citing an ID, including inside ranges")
    p.add_argument("id")
    p.add_argument("--scope", default="record", help="record | current | rationale | trail | memlog | all")
    p.add_argument("--children", action="store_true", help="include positional children (FR-7 → FR-7.k)")
    p.add_argument("--kind", choices=("mentions", "binds", "elaborates", "covers"), help="only this edge kind")
    p.add_argument("--page", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--size", type=int, default=60)
    p = sub.add_parser("search", help="ranked full-text search over sections and rows")
    p.add_argument("query", nargs="+")
    p.add_argument("--scope", default="record")
    p.add_argument("-k", type=int, default=5, help="number of hits")
    p.add_argument("--expand", type=int, default=0, help="include full text of the top N hits")
    from . import maintenance
    maintenance.add_commands(sub)
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    project = (args.project or find_project_root(Path.cwd())).resolve()
    overlay = args.overlay or (project / DEFAULT_OVERLAY if (project / DEFAULT_OVERLAY).is_file() else None)
    try:
        config = load(project, args.profile, overlay)
    except (ConfigError, OSError) as error:
        print(f"specdex: configuration error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_CONFIG
    for attempt in range(2):
        try:
            index = open_index(config, args.rev, args.db)
            try:
                return run(args, Queries(index))
            finally:
                index.conn.close()  # ends the read snapshot before a retry opens a fresh one
        except StaleIndex as error:
            if attempt:
                print(f"specdex: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
                return EXIT_USAGE
        except NotFound as error:
            print(f"specdex: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
            return EXIT_USAGE
        except (SourceError, ConfigError) as error:
            print(f"specdex: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
            return EXIT_CONFIG
    return EXIT_USAGE


def emit(args, value, text: str) -> None:
    print(render.to_json(value) if args.json else text)


def run(args, q: Queries) -> int:
    generation = q.index.generation
    if args.command == "status":
        status = q.status()
        emit(args, status, render.status_text(status))
    elif args.command == "outline":
        files = q.outline(args.target, args.level)
        emit(args, files, render.outline_text(files, generation))
    elif args.command == "resolve":
        resolution = q.resolve(" ".join([args.id]), with_text=args.text)
        emit(args, resolution, render.resolution_text(resolution, generation))
        return EXIT_OK if resolution.status == "defined" else EXIT_FINDINGS
    elif args.command == "get":
        hits, notes = [], []
        for ref in args.ref:
            found, more = q.get(ref, args.budget * CHARS_PER_TOKEN)
            hits += found
            notes += more
        emit(args, {"hits": hits, "notes": notes, "generation": generation}, render.hits_text(hits, notes, generation))
    elif args.command == "refs":
        resolution, rows, empty = q.refs(args.id, args.scope, args.children, args.kind)
        emit(args, {"resolution": resolution, "lines": rows, "empty": empty, "generation": generation},
             render.refs_text(resolution, rows, empty, args.page, args.size, generation))
    elif args.command == "search":
        hits, empty = q.search(" ".join(args.query), args.scope, args.k)
        for hit in hits[: args.expand]:
            q.verify_live(hit.path)
            hit.text = q.text(hit.path, hit.start, hit.end)
        notes = [f"no hits: {empty}"] if empty else []
        emit(args, {"hits": hits, "notes": notes, "generation": generation}, render.hits_text(hits, notes, generation))
    else:
        from . import maintenance
        return maintenance.run(args, q)
    return EXIT_OK

### AD-16: Signed artifacts, signed device items, and the last good one stays

- **Binds:** FR-45, FR-51, FR-64, FR-68, FR-69, FR-71, FR-93, FR-94, FR-96, FR-98, NFR-12
- **Prevents:** unsigned or untested content reaching devices; a compromised online key signing content or models; replayed or misdirected device items; a stale fetch changing what the child sees; old apps choking on new formats.
- **Rule:**
  - **One envelope** in `:core:contract`: `{typ, kid, iat, exp, aud, schemaMajor, payload, sig}`. The signature covers a canonical protected header (all fields except `sig`) plus the exact payload bytes, JWS-style. The key class is checked against the signed `typ`.
  - **Each type verifies only against its own key class:**

    | `typ` | Keys | What it is |
    |---|---|---|
    | `config`, `content_pack`, `model_manifest` | Offline artifact keys | Global artifacts. The configuration carries the guaranteed date, notices, and content and list versions |
    | `device_item` | The records service's online key, one key per purpose | A per-device item (AD-26). It must carry `exp`, `aud` (the link-check value or nonce it answers) and the link counter, and it is bound to the link secret. Replays and expired items are rejected |

  - **Keys.** The next key for each class ships in the app ahead of rotation. Each artifact type has its own key class.
  - **Bad or unknown input.** On a failed fetch, a bad signature or an unknown `schemaMajor`, the last good artifact stays. Fetch age alone never changes the child view; caps, consent, security restrictions and the guaranteed date still apply on their own terms. With no good file, the bundled defaults apply; an extension not received is never assumed (ACR-B).
  - **Per-device items** in the link-check response deliver web unlinks and record-deletion notices, never the global configuration (ACR-O). A web unlink or record deletion reaches the device at its next successful link check (FR-68.4).
  - **Publishing.** Content-bearing artifacts are published only with a passing evaluation record (AD-29).
  - **The guaranteed date's** single source is the signed configuration. The device keeps the latest date it has seen.
  - **Fetching.** Online devices fetch the configuration at most daily and at least every 30 days when connectivity permits, from our records host; it carries no device credential. Linked devices also run the link check, which sends only its single-use link-check value and allowed protocol metadata, never the server credential or link ID (ACR-O) `[ASSUMPTION: CQ-32]`.

#### FR-7: Basic mode

Every device runs basic mode with no brain, no consent, and only the traffic FR-7.3 lists. It includes care actions, play, the room, sleep, tap-teach, word cards, keepsakes, the diary, and dreams. Realizes UJ-2, UJ-5, UJ-12.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Basic mode runs:
  - before the unlock, and after a refund;
  - on the server tier while offline, before consent, after consent is revoked, while the server is unavailable, after the talk allowance is used up, and after the guaranteed date;
  - on the on-device tier while the model downloads, and after the parent removes it.
- Every basic-mode feature passes its tests with networking disabled.
- In basic mode, the device sends nothing except:
  - the service-configuration fetch (FR-94, no stable identifier) and, on a linked device, the link check (FR-94);
  - what a parent chose to send or request in the parent area (FR-64, FR-68, FR-69.1, FR-70–FR-72, FR-74, FR-86, FR-87, FR-102, FR-103);
  - model downloads (FR-95);
  - server-credential requests by an unlocked device (FR-88);
  - the US referral count (FR-104);
  - store traffic (Google Play purchases and age signal).

  Each exception follows its own authorization and retention rules, and child speech is never sent in basic mode. A request a parent makes offline is sent only when a connection returns. Counters and crash reports need the parent's opt-in `[ASSUMPTION: CQ-21]`. Credential requests need the unlock and active consent.
- Before the unlock, an ear tap plays a playful non-verbal reaction; the ear never glows, because the microphone never opens.

**Notes:** `[NOTE FOR PM]` If the talk-lite spike succeeds (OQ-6, OQ-18), basic mode could add offline recognition of words the child has already taught. That would be a later, additive change.
